newsitem.title: UK: UK Berlusconi papers transfer expected Friday.
newsitem.headline: UK Berlusconi papers transfer expected Friday.

text.p: Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said on Friday it expects the transfer of documents concerning business tycoon Silvio Berlusconi to proceed, possibly as early as later today.

The papers, which have been subject to protracted legal wrangling in the English courts over the past six months, will be sent to the Italian authorities investigating allegations of fraud and false accounting.

In a High Court hearing on Friday, Lord Justice Simon Brown said he did not believe the appellants - Berlusconi, his company Fininvest and company president Fedele Confalonieri - had grounds for a further appeal to the House of Lords.
But the judge did agree to certificate certain points of law which meant that lawyers representing Berlusconi could still apply for a further appeal.
At the same time, Brown said he could see no reason to stop the immediate transfer of the papers to Italy.
Legal sources said ity was extremely unlikely that leave to appeal to the Lords would be granted in these circumstances.
Elizabeth Roberts of law firm Peters and Peters, who have represented Berlusconi, said Friday's hearing had been disappointing but that the position was still being reviewed.

On Wednesday, Brown rejected an appeal by Berlusconi over the papers which the judge said were linked to fraud and false accounting allegations amounting to 51 million pounds ($82 million) which had been "surreptitiously removed from Fininvest and used for criminal purposes."
Prosecutions were already underway in Italy against Berlusconi for bribing Revenue inspectors and for making illicit donations to former Prime Minister Bettino Craxi.
Italian investigators suspect Berlusconi who owns three TV channels as well as football club AC Milan, may have used offshore companies to channel payments to politicians.
